description: Macedonian rulers became hegemon over Greece primarily through the military and diplomatic successes of Philip II of Macedon in the 4th century BC. Philip reorganized the Macedonian army around the sarissa-armed phalanx, powerful cavalry, and professional siege forces, then combined conquest, alliances, marriage diplomacy, and political pressure to expand his influence over the Greek city-states. His decisive victory over Athens and Thebes at Chaeronea in 338 BC broke the strongest organized resistance, after which he established the League of Corinth, placing most of Greece under Macedonian leadership while allowing the poleis a degree of internal autonomy. Alexander the Great inherited this hegemonic system and used it as the political and military foundation for his conquest of the Persian Empire.
requirementsTooltip: Unlocked in Empire Phase when a Macedonian or Epirote player captures a non-Macedonian or non-Epirote Civic Center.
